Description: One row per vendor onboarding request raised by a buyer in the supplier registration queue. request_id; raised_on (date the buyer raised it, mixed date formats); raised_by and raised_by_email (the buyer); company_code (SAP company code) and plant (SAP plant code, listed in 00_INDEX); category (purchase category code); business_need (buyer's free text); vendor_name_as_typed (the vendor's name exactly as the buyer typed it, which can be informal); vendor_contact_name, vendor_contact_email, vendor_contact_phone (contact the buyer gave); constitution_declared, state_declared, city_declared, msme_declared (Y/N), gst_registered_declared (Y/N): what the vendor declared on the registration form; estimated_annual_spend_inr (mixed number formats); slp_registration_id (supplier registration portal reference); status (Documents awaited or Documents received, as maintained by the desk).

Which documents each vendor must provide, by constitution, category and declaration. requirement_id; applies_to (the condition); document; mandatory (Yes/No); accepted_forms (what is accepted in its place, if anything); validity_check (what makes the document acceptable); fields_cross_checked (values that must agree with other documents).

The verification rule set the onboarding desk applies, one row per rule. rule_id; area; rule; applies_to; evidence (documents the rule reads); if_not_met (what the desk does). The same rules with the chase cadence and holiday calendar are in reference/Verification_Rule_Set.md and .pdf.

Extract of existing vendors from the SAP S/4HANA business partner master (vendor role). LIFNR (vendor number); NAME1 and NAME2 (name, split at 35 characters); SORTL (search term); STRAS, ORT01, REGIO, PSTLZ, LAND1 (street, city, region, PIN, country); TELF1 (phone); SMTP_ADDR (email); J_1IPANNO (PAN); STCD3 (GSTIN); BANKS, BANKL, BANKN, KOINH (bank country, IFSC, account number, account holder); MSME_FLAG and UDYAM_NO; KTOKK (account group); CATEGORY; ERDAT (created on, dd.mm.yyyy); SPERR (X = blocked for posting); LOEVM (X = marked for deletion); BUKRS_EXTENDED (company codes the vendor is extended to). Older records can have blank PAN or GSTIN.

Every document checklist and chase the onboarding desk has sent so far. log_id; request_id; action (Document checklist sent, Chase 1, Chase 2); round (0, 1, 2); sent_at (timestamps are IST unless they carry a Z for UTC); sent_by; sent_to; cc; items_requested (the full text sent); thread_id and message_id (link to the mailbox; vendor replies carry this message_id in In-Reply-To).

Register of attachments the desk has filed from the onboarding mailbox. request_id; received_at (IST); from_address; mailbox_file (the .eml the file came in); attachment_name (as sent); stored_as (path under documents/, renamed with a number only when a name repeats); pages; size_kb. The register does not say what each file is: some files hold several documents and some are scans.

Complete and consistent document sets; sets that arrive across several emails, as merged PDFs or as scans; names that differ only in suffix, case or an M/s prefix; names on the bank proof, Udyam or incorporation certificate that differ by one word or carry an earlier company name; PAN on the PAN document that differs from the PAN inside the GSTIN; GSTIN state code that disagrees with the principal place of business or the declared state; GSTINs that fail the check character; certificates that have lapsed, that lapse within a month, and lapsed certificates sent with a renewal receipt that may or may not meet the rule; illegible scans; MSME declared without a Udyam certificate; bank proofs that are unsigned, unprinted or carry a malformed IFSC; proprietors whose bank account is in the proprietor's own name; vendors not registered under GST; vendors with more than one GST registration; vendors already on the master under a different spelling, including blocked and legacy records; existing vendors registering a new state; vendors that have not replied, that replied only with an auto reply, or that stopped replying after the first chase; records that combine two of these; and records that look irregular but are in order.
